questions.q: What is the difference between a Full Refresh and an Incremental Refresh?
options: There is no functional difference — they're the same operation
Incremental Refresh deletes the extract entirely
Full Refresh is faster than Incremental Refresh in every case
Full Refresh re-pulls everything from scratch; Incremental Refresh appends only new rows since the last refresh based on a chosen column
questions.explain: Full Refresh discards and rebuilds the whole extract; Incremental Refresh only appends new rows, usually much faster for large append-only data.

options: A log of every refresh, with a timestamp, action (e.g. Full refresh), and row count
A list of every user who has viewed the workbook
The original SQL query used to build the extract
A history of every calculated field ever created
questions.explain: Extract History logs each refresh event with its timestamp, the action taken, and how many rows were involved — useful for troubleshooting stale data.

questions.q: What happens when the .hyper file behind an extract is moved or deleted?
options: Tableau converts the connection to Live without asking
Tableau shows an 'Extract Not Found' dialog with recovery options, rather than failing silently
Tableau automatically deletes the whole workbook
The workbook opens normally with no indication anything changed
questions.explain: Tableau surfaces an explicit Extract Not Found dialog rather than silently failing or guessing what to do.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four recovery options in the Extract Not Found dialog?
options: Publish to Tableau Server automatically
Remove the extract
Regenerate the extract
Locate the extract
questions.explain: The four real options are Locate, Remove, Deactivate, and Regenerate the extract — publishing to Server automatically isn't one of them.

questions.q: Why does the column chosen for an Incremental Refresh usually need to only increase (like a date or an auto-incrementing ID)?
options: So Tableau can reliably identify which rows are new since the last refresh, without re-scanning the whole source
Because incremental refreshes ignore that column entirely
It has no bearing on how incremental refresh works
Because Tableau requires all columns to be numeric
questions.explain: An ever-increasing column (date, auto-incrementing ID) lets Tableau reliably identify and append only the new rows since the last refresh.
